doc.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Nellie Lutcher and Lambert, Hendricks & Ross
title: How Lambert, Hendricks & Ross came together
summary: He explains what he understands of the group's origins and its members' backgrounds.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Right. Well tell me how Lambert, Hendricks & Ross came about.

Well from what I understand, I was their second drummer. I took Walter Bolden’s place. That was after they had recorded their first Columbia album “The Hottest New Group in Jazz.” From what I understand Jon had moved to New York, Dave had lived here, I’m not sure if he was from here but he had lived here, and he wrote, I’m sure it’s fairly common knowledge that he wrote the arrangements for Charlie Parker’s “Old Folks,” the vocal arrangements and a few others. And on the record I think the vocal group is called The Dave Lambert Singers. And so he was known for vocal writing and I guess organizing choral groups, jazz oriented choral groups, and Jon I think had just moved to New York not too long before he and Dave met up. I’m not sure how they met up. I think maybe it could have come from Annie influencing Dave through her vocalese work, “Twisted,” I think she had done that on the west coast with Wardell Gray and Art Farmer I think. And she was the niece of Ella Logan, the Hollywood actress, and Annie was British — well I think she had dual citizenship. But at any rate she spent her childhood here in LA, in the movies, she was in the “Our Gang” comedies. She was one of the “Our Gang” kids. And I think she more or less grew up in LA and Hollywood, and pretty much she became a jazz singer. And then I guess she moved to New York I guess in the middle 50s or whatever. I’m not sure how that whole stuff coalesced, but they — it’s been written about.
